answer.rationale: Write-path p99 began climbing ~30 minutes after the release shipped, making the new build the leading suspect; memory_b1 supports rollback as a fast, write-safe recovery, and I want to confirm its source record before acting. I also verify memory_b3 because settlement peak traffic is a plausible confounder — if the archived record shows headroom provisioning resolved a similar surge, add_capacity could be the safer choice since rollback during peak writes carries its own risk. Circuit breakers and read-replica routing target dependency outages and read load respectively, neither of which matches a write-path regression; failover does not address a code-induced latency climb. Chosen action is conditional on verification: if b1's record confirms a comparable release-correlated write-path spike resolved cleanly by rollback, proceed; if evidence instead points to pure capacity saturation, switch to add_capacity.
